name: essence-language
description: Language support for Essence: syntax highlighting, diagnostics, navigation, completion and debugging.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The bundled Language Server only reads and analyses text, and diagnostics and navigation are exactly what is wanted while auditing an unfamiliar repository, so they stay on. The trust-sensitive settings are 'essence.server.path' and 'essence.cli.path': each names an executable to spawn, which a workspace could point at a program it ships itself, so workspace-scoped values of them are ignored here. Debugging itself is unavailable in Restricted Mode either way — VS Code blocks debug sessions there.

scripts.build: bun run build:server && bun run build:extension

essence.server.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a Language Server to run instead of the bundled one. A built `.js` bundle is run with `node`; anything else — a `.ts` entry point, or `packages/language-server/bin/esls` — is run with `bun`. Useful for developing against a checkout of the Essence monorepo without rebuilding the bundle.

essence.trace.server.description: Log the traffic between VS Code and the Essence Language Server.

essence.cli.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `essence` CLI the debugger compiles with. A built `.js` bundle is run with `node`; anything else — a checkout's `packages/cli/bin/essence` — is run with `bun`. Left empty, a checkout open in the workspace is used if one is found, and `essence` on PATH otherwise.

program.description: The .es source file to compile and debug.

cwd.description: The working directory the program runs in.

env.description: Environment variables set for the program.

stopOnEntry.description: Pause on the first statement the program's own source wrote.

runtimeExecutable.description: The executable that runs the compiled JavaScript. Debugging requires Node — the adapter speaks its inspector protocol.

glueFrames.description: What becomes of compiler-generated stack frames: hidden entirely, or shown greyed out.

keepArtifacts.description: Keep the compiled JavaScript and its map after the session, and say where they are.

artifact.description: A precompiled bundle to debug instead of compiling 'program' — its source map must sit beside it.

configurationSnippets.label: Essence: Launch
configurationSnippets.description: Compile an Essence source file and debug it
